label: Apple picking
summary: Apple picking is a user behaviour identified by Nielsen and Norman in a study on early generative AI interactions. It describes the pattern where a user wants to reuse previously generated content, either as context for a new prompt or as the actual text to be changed, in order to produce a new iteration. The linear structure of conversational interfaces makes this non-linear task particularly cumbersome.
how_maaike_uses: Maaike introduces apple picking as part of her broader critique of writing with AI tools like Jasper.ai and ChatGPT. She uses it to name and validate the frustrating review-regenerate-repeat loop she experienced herself on a Sunday afternoon writing session. Her specific angle is that conversational interfaces are structurally ill-suited to non-linear tasks like writing and editing, and the apple picking behaviour is evidence of that mismatch rather than a quirk of individual users.
open_questions: The passage is cut off mid-sentence when describing the scrolling problem in conversational interfaces, so the full extent of the limitation as Maaike sees it is not fully captured.
It is not clear from the material whether Maaike thinks the articulation barrier is solvable within conversational interfaces, or whether it points to a more fundamental problem with the format.
